topic: Sharp connected-interval decision frontier at the hidden-treatment causal-null fiber. In the fixed-J iid Gaussian-outcome, binary-surrogate, binary-negative-control hidden-treatment model with compact ordered mechanisms and known shrinking effect radius, solve the product Gaussian posterior-contrast-fiber decision problem: characterize the minimax worst-case expected length among honest connected intervals by a least-favorable saddle, give certified convergent primal-dual computation and an attaining rule, derive the exact regret of the explicitly coverage-calibrated profile-distance hull including zero-regret conditions and a legal strict-positive-regret regime, and lift the rule uniformly to moving iid nuisance fibers and active constraint cones. Recover centered Gaussian efficiency only when sqrt(n) times every outcome gap and every declared regularity slack diverges. Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen arXiv:2405.09080v4 is the off-null anchor and its ADNI section 8 is a prospective reanalysis consumer; credit Zwiernik--Smith for tripod inversion, Drton/Andrews--Cheng/Cox/Schlemper--Moreira for generic singular and weak-ID machinery, and Evans--Hansen--Stark for bounded-normal optimal intervals. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the randomized endpoint-kernel primal and two-measure dual, reduced the positive q=(.31,.19,.19,.31) null fiber to an exact curved two-parameter Gaussian mean surface, and reduced the legal q=(.41,.09,.09,.41) active face to bounded normal location with scale sqrt(8/41), where strict Neyman--Pearson/Evans--Hansen--Stark duality implies positive profile regret for 0<sqrt(8/41)rho<=2z_.95. It verified profile-hull honesty and checked empty inversions, endpoint randomization, radius faces, topology changes, and interior margins; no same-theorem collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove uniform local asymptotic equivalence of the iid hidden-treatment experiment, including moving nuisance fibers and every active cone, strongly enough to transfer coverage and expected length of an attaining randomized connected interval. EARLY KILL TEST: On q=(.31,.19,.19,.31), epsilon=.1, sigma=1, and rho in {1,2,4}, run nested certified primal-upper and atomic-dual-lower programs over the exact fiber with tail and endpoint-dither errors; pivot if the certified gap does not decrease or continuum coverage cannot be certified. open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact minimax worst-case expected length of honest randomized connected intervals on the curved hidden-treatment causal-null Gaussian fiber, and when does the coverage-calibrated profile-distance hull have zero rather than strictly positive regret?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Zhou–Tchetgen Tchetgen excludes the causal-null point, where binary-tripod inversion develops a nuisance fiber rather than a regular inverse. Evans–Hansen–Stark solves restricted scalar location problems, not a curved Gaussian mean surface with unidentified nuisance and the nonconvex requirement that each reported set be connected. The prior donor-face calculation independently demonstrates that an honest profile-type hull can have a substantial strict decision-risk gap. New work must couple acceptance decisions across effect values through randomized endpoints, establish strong duality against least-favorable measures on the actual fiber, and characterize when the profile acceptance family coincides with that saddle.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A primal-dual saddle equality with measurable attaining endpoint kernels, an explicit regret functional for the calibrated profile hull, necessary-and-sufficient zero-regret conditions, and a legal active-face submodel on which a strict Neyman–Pearson inequality proves positive regret over a stated radius range.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its direct comparison of uniformly covering restricted-parameter intervals through worst-case expected length and strict regret against familiar competitors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Parameter restrictions permit shorter honest intervals -> standard truncation or profiling uses the restriction without optimizing length -> least-favorable duality identifies the optimal rule -> determine when the hidden-treatment profile hull coincides with or falls short of that rule.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent confidence procedures as randomized acceptance kernels, derive a Bayes-minimax saddle, and use likelihood-ratio ordering with randomized boundary decisions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is the connected-interval, curved-fiber analogue of its restricted-location saddle and attaining rule.

method_exemplars.technique: Use moment coordinates and the product-form tripod parametrization to invert regular strata and explicitly parameterize singular observational fibers.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The binary surrogate, negative control, and hidden treatment form a tripod whose null fiber indexes the Gaussian decision problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Recover weak-identification confidence sets by exact root geometry or controlled approximation rather than uncertified grid inversion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact profile regret requires recovering every endpoint and topology change of the comparator hull before comparing its expected length.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the fixed-J hidden-treatment iid experiment be reduced uniformly over moving causal-null nuisance fibers, all outcome-gap rates, and every active compact-mechanism constraint cone to its product-Gaussian contrast-fiber experiment strongly enough to transfer randomized connected-interval coverage and worst-case expected length?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing results divide the task among off-null semiparametric inference, generic drifting-strength quadratic expansions, boundary-aware minimum-distance limits, and pointwise tangent-cone asymptotics. None controls Le Cam deficiency uniformly over nuisance-indexed fibers whose topology and active inequalities change. The prior panel attempt shows why weak convergence of a selected statistic is insufficient: coverage is discontinuous and interval length is unbounded, requiring boundary control and uniform integrability. The adjacent proximal run separately leaves score lifting unresolved when nuisance kernels move. The hidden-treatment proof must therefore construct QMD score lifts and comparison kernels on each active cone while remaining uniform as the fiber itself moves.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform deficiency-distance or direct risk-transfer theorem with explicit localization and tail bounds, plus a transfer lemma preserving worst-case coverage and expected length for boundedly truncated randomized connected intervals and a uniform-integrability argument removing the truncation.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from hidden-treatment identification to efficient inference makes the loss of regularity at vanishing relevance the natural motivation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Surrogate and proxy measurements identify hidden-treatment effects under relevance -> fixed margins permit efficient root-n inference -> local sequences approaching the causal-null fiber invalidate that approximation -> uniform experiment equivalence is needed for honest decision-optimal intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Index drifting identification sequences, prove stochastic quadratic expansions uniformly over subsequences, and exhaust weak, semi-strong, and strong regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired equivalence must likewise hold across every rate at which outcome relevance vanishes, but at the stronger experiment and decision-risk level.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine weak-identification localization with boundary cones and retain inequality information in identification-robust confidence procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Compact ordered mechanisms create moving active inequality cones simultaneously with weak identification.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace a regular tangent space by the correct semialgebraic tangent cone and derive the associated Gaussian distance limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Gaussian contrast-fiber experiment must use the correct active cone at each nuisance point before risk transfer can be valid.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a terminating certified primal-dual algorithm for the continuum hidden-treatment fiber interval problem whose primal upper bounds and atomic-dual lower bounds converge with explicit tail, mesh, coverage, and endpoint-randomization error certificates across topology changes and active faces?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Evans–Hansen–Stark supplies the infinite-dimensional dual but not certified two-sided approximation on curved semialgebraic fibers with connected endpoints. Schlemper–Moreira handles structured polynomial or rational inversion, whereas this problem combines Gaussian integration, continuum coverage constraints, endpoint dithering, and mechanism inequalities. Two prior CausalSmith runs also reached continuum Gaussian calibration problems without converting them into terminating evaluations. A finite grid alone provides neither continuum honesty nor a lower certificate, and least-favorable support can jump when the fiber changes topology.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A nested pair of finite programs whose primal values decrease and atomic-dual values increase to the same saddle value, with a rule and computable certificates for between-grid coverage, Gaussian-tail loss, endpoint-dither loss, semialgebraic feasibility, and termination at any requested tolerance.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames numerical inversion errors as inferential failures and makes auditable computation part of the statistical contribution.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Weak identification produces complicated confidence sets -> ordinary grids can omit components and invalidate coverage -> structure-aware inversion restores reliability -> curved hidden-treatment fibers require analogous primal-dual certificates.

method_exemplars.technique: Discretize the randomized-test primal while retaining finite-support least-favorable measures as dual lower certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested upper and lower programs approximate precisely its confidence-kernel decision dual.

method_exemplars.technique: Control inversion error through root isolation or increasing-degree approximation and translate numerical error into coverage error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same obligation arises here, with Gaussian quadrature and fiber meshes replacing polynomial critical-value approximation.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode the latent-tree image with moment equalities and positivity-induced inequalities and stratify its boundary faces.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Certified optimization must range over the legal hidden-treatment fiber rather than an equality-only algebraic relaxation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted proxy-effect-law run controls effect collisions only under fixed latent-arm probability and proxy singular-value floors; its review withholds inference on the full weak-margin class. Zhou–Tchetgen Tchetgen likewise assumes every relevant probability and latent-class contrast is separated by one fixed positive constant. Generic weak-ID classifications do not determine how simultaneous deterioration of outcome relevance, proxy rank, positivity, and active ordering inequalities affects optimal interval length. The fixed-margin Lipschitz inverse must be replaced by a multirate local modulus and cone experiment with same-class lower bounds.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise minimax expected-length characterization and attaining honest interval indexed by the vector of root-n-scaled gaps and slacks, including an if-and-only-if result that the centered semiparametric efficient Gaussian interval is recovered exactly when every scaled coordinate diverges and explicit cone-truncated or fiber-mixture limits otherwise.

writing_exemplar.why: Its weak, semi-strong, and strong identification narrative is the closest template for presenting a complete multirate phase diagram.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Standard inference works under strong identification -> drifting strength creates transitional and weak regimes -> uniform validity requires exhausting all sequences -> hidden-treatment efficiency depends jointly on every outcome-gap and mechanism-slack sequence.

method_exemplars.technique: Express the nonregular causal target as a nonlinear map of minimal sufficient regular reduced-form coordinates and isolate their Gaussian information.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Observable hidden-treatment contrasts remain regular even when their inverse map to the causal effect becomes singular.

method_exemplars.technique: Classify arbitrary drifting sequences by normalized identification strength and prove regime-specific limits through exhaustive subsequence arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed frontier requires both regular-regime recovery and failure of centered efficiency whenever any scaled gap remains bounded.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute local semialgebraic tangent cones and derive Gaussian distance laws that change with the active boundary stratum.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Complementary regimes depend not only on weak outcome contrasts but also on which mechanism inequalities bind.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The failed proximal run isolates the relevant distinction: an algebraic null fiber need not be the image of nonnegative latent causal completions, but its proposed witness was invalid and its certificate collapsed into generic feasibility. For the hidden-treatment destination, the first proof step changes from a linear bridge-null response-type table to a polynomial tripod map with ordering, positivity, and compact-radius constraints. A resolution must establish stratumwise local surjectivity or exhibit complete observed laws and a separating certificate showing that profile optimization over the algebraic fiber is causally too wide.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an equality characterization of algebraic and legal contrast fibers under explicit rank and interior conditions, or a verified finite separating example with endpoint-attaining legal mechanisms, unequal sharp contrast intervals, and a dual infeasibility certificate.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing separates nonuniqueness of nuisance bridge solutions from identification of the causal functional, which is the conceptual precursor to algebraic-versus-legal fibers.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Proxy equations may have many solutions -> a causal functional can remain invariant on the algebraic solution set -> algebraic invariance does not itself establish latent-mechanism realizability -> characterize the legal hidden-treatment contrast fiber.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode finite latent response types as nonnegative weights, optimize the causal functional over compatible completions, and certify sharp endpoints by duality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Legal-fiber endpoints require analogous latent-completion and separation logic, extended from a polytope to ordered polynomial mechanisms.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert solvability tests for systems whose coefficients are estimated and control behavior near feasibility boundaries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once legal-fiber membership is computable, endpoint inference must propagate sampling error through that feasibility problem.

literature_map:
Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (arXiv:2405.09080v4) identify hidden-treatment causal effects from a surrogate and proxy and derive efficient, multiply robust inference.
Their relevance condition explicitly rules out the causal null, and their fixed-margin asymptotics stop before the proposed null-fiber decision problem.
Their ADNI analysis supplies a concrete consumer, estimating the effect of Alzheimer’s disease on hippocampal volume using latent disease status and observed cognitive proxies.
Zwiernik and Smith (Bernoulli 2012, arXiv:1004.4360) provide moment-coordinate inversion for binary latent trees and describe unidentified fibers as cornered geometric objects.
Zwiernik and Smith (EJS 2011, arXiv:0904.1980) show that positivity-induced inequalities are indispensable because equality invariants alone can admit infeasible mechanisms.
Drton (Annals of Statistics 2009, arXiv:math/0703360) establishes tangent-cone likelihood limits at semialgebraic boundaries and singularities.
Andrews and Cheng (Econometrica 2012, DOI 10.3982/ECTA9456) give uniform weak, semi-strong, and strong identification theory for stochastic-quadratic criterion models.
Cox (arXiv:2012.11222) combines weak identification with parameter bounds and boundary limit theory, but not latent-fiber decision optimality.
Kaji (Econometrica 2021, DOI 10.3982/ECTA16413) treats weakly regular parameters as degree-zero maps of regular reduced forms and develops weak efficiency.
Evans, Hansen, and Stark (Bernoulli 2005, DOI 10.3150/bj/1126126761) solve minimax expected-measure confidence-set problems through randomized-test and Bayes-minimax duality.
Their bounded-normal analysis supplies the active-face benchmark and shows that honest conventional or truncated intervals can have strict expected-length regret.
Schafer and Stark (JASA 2009, DOI 10.1198/jasa.2009.tm07420) approximate minimax expected-size confidence regions on compact spaces, but do not give the requested deterministic two-sided continuum certificate.
Schlemper and Moreira (arXiv:2604.04279) show that grid inversion under weak identification can omit components or truncate sets, motivating certified computation.
The scan found no primary paper combining hidden-treatment null-fiber geometry, connected-interval minimax length, certified primal-dual computation, and uniform iid-to-Gaussian risk transfer over moving active cones.
